metadata.title: Transparent Limitations, Known Boundaries, and Negative Results
metadata.sprint: Final 8-Hour Sprint: Reliability and Research Showcase

negative_findings.hypothesis: Model possesses algorithmic primality testing via learned code logic.
negative_findings.empirical_reality: Model learned a superficial parity heuristic (is_prime := n % 2 != 0). Scores 59.46% on balanced sets by classifying all even numbers as composite, but fails on all odd composites (9, 15, 25, 49) and Carmichael numbers (561, 1105).
negative_findings.recommendation: Do not claim genuine mathematical reasoning capability; state clearly that small models require external tools for reliable arithmetic.

negative_findings.hypothesis: Model autonomously distinguishes between Python and Web Researcher when both are enabled.
negative_findings.empirical_reality: Heavy inductive prior toward Python tool due to 10:1 representation in Stage 1 training data. Frequently calls Python even on factual lookup tasks unless Web tool is isolated.
negative_findings.recommendation: Use routing guards or balanced two-tool fine-tuning in future work.

negative_findings.hypothesis: Model critically validates tool observation against user question.
negative_findings.empirical_reality: Model faithfully ingests and reports tool observation, but treats buggy script outputs as ground truth without self-correction.
negative_findings.recommendation: Closed-loop synthesis should be audited by downstream verification modules.

negative_findings.hypothesis: Broad multi-tool schema training enables zero-shot tool usage.
negative_findings.empirical_reality: Providing extensive multi-page schema documentation with only 0.69% authentic execution examples caused model to treat schemas as conversational text, resulting in 0% intent recall.
negative_findings.recommendation: Compact manifests with authentic input-execution-observation supervision are strictly required.
